action: As the airline's notice urges, reported by Airways Magazine, ShebaMiles members should watch for suspicious or unsolicited communications about their account.
date_note: Date of the airline's customer notice; the intrusion date was not stated.
exec: A national airline has told frequent-flyer customers their information may have been affected; passenger loyalty data is a ready phishing source.
plain: Ethiopian Airlines told ShebaMiles frequent-flyer members that certain customer information may have been affected. It says there is no evidence financial information was accessed; the scale is not yet clear.

sources.name: CIO Africa (relaying Reuters and Addis Fortune)

summary: Ethiopian Airlines notified ShebaMiles members on 18 November of a limited-scope incident that may have affected certain customer information, with no evidence financial information was accessed; CEO Mesfin Tasew confirmed an investigation to Reuters, which said the scale was not immediately clear. Airways Magazine, relaying Addis Fortune, says commercial chief Lemma Yadecha said suspicious activity was detected on 17 November, the intrusion was contained, and data and miles were not taken or altered.
title: Ethiopian Airlines reports ShebaMiles frequent-flyer data incident

validation.note: Notice reported by Capital Ethiopia and Fidel Post; Reuters (via TimesLIVE) reports the notice and the CEO confirming an investigation. Follow-up 22 Nov: Airways Magazine says an account-count estimate in Addis Fortune carries an editor's note that Ethiopian had not officially confirmed it, so the earlier figure of fewer than 8,000 accounts was removed; Lemma Yadecha's statements are relayed from Addis Fortune, which was not read. TechCabal (403) not read.
